key_insight: Compared with conventional APS, axial-fed supersonic HV-APS produced Cr₃C₂–NiCr coatings with nearly half the porosity and 27% lower sliding wear volume, but little improvement in normal-impact erosion.
engineering_relevance: HV-APS is promising for denser, harder coatings on steel components exposed to sliding wear, while its benefit under 90° erosive impact remains limited.
method: Sprayed Metco 5241 powder onto S235 steel using radial-fed APS and axial-fed supersonic HV-APS.
Compared coating microstructure, phase composition, porosity, and microhardness.
Evaluated 90° impact erosion and ball-on-disc sliding wear at 30 N.
evidence_signal: HV-APS versus APS yielded 6.16% versus 11.99% porosity, 1141 versus 897 HV0.2 hardness, 2.85 versus 3.90 mm³ sliding wear volume, and 0.19 versus 0.20 mg/g specific erosion rate.
watch_item: Torch design, flow regime, and powder-feed geometry changed together, so the improvements cannot be attributed to axial feeding alone.
paper_title: Microstructure and wear properties of Cr₃C₂–NiCr coatings sprayed by conventional and supersonic high-velocity atmospheric plasma spraying with axial powder feeding
